reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
convert an IN subquery to a semi-join
reached_sql:
SELECT nd.d_year, it.i_brand_id AS brand_id, it.i_brand AS brand, SUM(fg.daily_sum) AS sum_agg
FROM (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_sold_date_sk, it.i_brand_id, it.i_brand, SUM(ss.ss_sales_price) AS daily_sum
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN (
        SELECT d_date_sk
        FROM date_dim
        WHERE d_moy = 11
    ) nd ON nd.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN (
        SELECT i_item_sk, i_brand_id, i_brand
        FROM item
        WHERE i_manufact_id = 816
    ) it ON it.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_sold_date_sk, it.i_brand_id, it.i_brand
) fg
JOIN (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_year
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy = 11
) nd ON nd.d_date_sk = fg.ss_sold_date_sk
GROUP BY nd.d_year, fg.i_brand_id, fg.i_brand
ORDER BY nd.d_year, sum_agg DESC, brand_id
LIMIT 100
reasoning_trace:
1. COVERING ITEM INDEX — TARGET: item.i_manufact_id = 816 — Add/use a covering index on item(i_manufact_id) INCLUDE (i_item_sk, i_brand_id, i_brand) so the handful of manufacturer-816 items and their brand fields become a tiny driving set without heap lookups.

2. ITEM-DRIVEN STORE_SALES LOOKUP — TARGET: store_sales.ss_item_sk with ss_sold_date_sk and ss_sales_price — Add/use a covering index on store_sales(ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk) INCLUDE (ss_sales_price) and probe store_sales only for the item keys from #1, avoiding both a 57.6M-row scan and a scan of all November sales.

3. NOVEMBER DATE SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk filtered by date_dim.d_moy = 11 — Apply the small set of November d_date_sk values as a filter on the item-limited store_sales rows, eliminating all non-November sales before aggregation.

4. PRE-AGGREGATE ITEM/DATE SUMS — TARGET: store_sales SUM(ss_sales_price) grouped by (ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk) — Collapse the filtered fact rows into one sum per item per sold date, sharply reducing the input to the final year/brand grouping.

5. POST-AGGREGATION DIMENSION JOIN — TARGET: join of the preaggregated result to date_dim and item — Join the tiny preaggregated rows to date_dim only for d_year and use the already-fetched item.i_brand_id/i_brand, then apply the final GROUP BY d_year, i_brand_id, i_brand and ORDER BY ... LIMIT 100 on only that small result.
